single molecule protein unfolding and stretching is possible by applying a voltage across a solid-state nanopores.
the protein domain can be unfolded by applying an increasing voltage across the pore and that the unfolding is dependent on the stability of the domain.
the unfolding of protein domains can be controlled by electric fields inside a solid-state nanometer-scale pore.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of single-molecule methods that can be used to study protein folding and unfolding in a controlled manner.
the use of a nanopore to stretch and unfold proteins in a controllable and reproducible manner.
the development of a new method to unfold and stretch protein domains inside solid-state nanopores.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the voltage mediated unfolding mechanism is a single molecule method that is capable of unfolding protein domains inside a nanopore and can provide a wealth of information about the stability and unfolding mechanism of a protein.
this method provides a unique opportunity to study the unfolding of protein domains at the single molecule level in a solid-state nanopores.
single molecule stretching experiments performed in a nanopore can provide a detailed understanding of the stability of a protein and its unfolding mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protein unfolding is a gradual process, which can be controlled by electric field and is dependent on the stability of the native state.
this method can unfold a protein in an electric field and is a function of its stability.
this method is capable of measuring the unfolding of a protein in a solid-state nanopores and that this unfolding is a function in both the applied voltage and the stability of the native protein.

a solid-state nanoporous device can be used as a platform to perform protein unfolding experiments and can provide new insights into protein stability.
